analysis.title: GS Sector Specialists: U.S. Industrials & Materials - FOMC, CTVA, VYLR, DAL (8 Oct 2026)
key_insights: US S&P futures were down 30bps pre-market, led lower by technology. Higher yields, higher oil, and a muted reaction to Samsung (down 300bps despite record profits) and TSMC weighed on risk appetite.
Overseas, KOSPI was down 260bps, Japan down 140bps, and Europe down 50-75bps. French geopolitical concerns are spreading to Italian and Greek sovereign risk.
Crude was up 4%, with Brent at $105 and WTI approaching $92, after a tanker was struck off Qatar. The desk notes attacks can extend beyond the immediate Strait of Hormuz.
The 10-year yield rose 4bps to local highs of 5.33%. DXY is above 102 and Bitcoin is down to $82.8k with broader risk appetite.

Cyclicals were hit harder on the day despite relief in rates and oil. Inbounds flagged CAT -6%, HUBG -7%, QXO -7% on heavy volume, CGNX -8%, ALLE -5% on competitive news, and GVA -5%. US cyclicals vs. the equal-weight S&P are back at lows.

The September FOMC minutes show all participants supported a 25bp hike to 3.75-4%, judging progress on lowering inflation as not sufficient. Almost all saw inflation risks tilted to the upside, and labor market risks as diminished and broadly balanced.

Most FOMC participants judged another increase would likely be appropriate by year end, while stressing each meeting would be approached with an open mind. GS expects the second hike in December but sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes further tightening is unnecessary.
With Warsh taking a different approach to the FOMC, the desk says the minutes are likely more important than historically.

DAL reports Friday Oct 9 pre-market at 6:30am (call at 10am) with a 6% implied move. The desk rates positioning 6-7/10. DAL has outperformed other travel names, consensus EPS is below the low end of guidance, and the buyside expects Q4 topline acceleration.

DAL full-year guidance is EPS $6.50-7.50 and free cash flow of $3-4bn. The Street is at EPS $5.89, below the low end, with Q4 revenue growth expected to accelerate to +17% y/y. Airline revenue trends are strong, but costs (fuel and ex-fuel) are worse. DAL is better protected, with higher margins and ownership of Trainer.

Duffy on CTVA after the Oct 1 spin-off of Vylor (VYLR, seed business, about two-thirds of old CTVA sales and EBITDA): CTVA trades at 9.2x EV/EBITDA on Q5-Q8 vs a 10.5x target multiple. GS sees a $20 price target, about 38% upside.

CTVA thesis: ag chem is a specialty business with patent, brand, formulation, labeling, and distribution protection. FMC is a poor comp (highly levered, large patent expiry, restructuring), and FMC traded at an average 9.1x EV/EBITDA in 2020-24 vs 7.7x now. GS uses $1.75bn of NPV in EV for PFAS and pension liabilities. Guidance midpoint implies about $600mn/yr FCF in 2027-29, a >6% FCF yield vs a 2.2% coverage average.

GS initiates VYLR at Buy with an $87 price target (+19%). Thesis: wide moats (top two seed companies, Vylor and Bayer, have held stable combined share for 25 years), about 4% revenue and 8% EBITDA base growth, hybrid wheat potential, gene-editing acceleration, an out-licensing model, and M&A optionality. GS argues 15-20x EBITDA (17.5x midpoint) is warranted.
Post-spin trading volume: about 62mn VYLR shares vs more than 465mn CTVA shares in the first five days.

market_movers.rationale: Market is mispricing CTVA around the spin. GS expects a re-rating from 9.2x to 10.5x EV/EBITDA over the next year, implying about 38% upside, with FCF yield above 6%.
Highest quality ag company with wide moats and about 4% revenue and 8% EBITDA base growth. GS argues for 15-20x EBITDA with a 17.5x base case, citing gene editing, licensing, and hybrid wheat.
Reports Oct 9 pre-market with a 6% implied move. Street EPS of $5.89 is below the low end of the $6.50-7.50 guide, but the stock has outperformed travel peers, which raises the bar.

sector_views.rationale: Cyclicals are weak, with US cyclicals vs. the equal-weight S&P back at lows. The desk fields inbounds on CAT, aerospace resilience, and building products.
GS sees CTVA and VYLR mispriced or deserving premium multiples after the spin, with Buy ratings on both.

earnings_insights: DAL reports Fri 10/9 pre-market (estimate, not yet reported). Street EPS consensus is $5.89, below the low end of company full-year guidance of $6.50-7.50. Company full-year FCF guidance is $3-4bn. Street Q4 revenue growth is expected at +17% y/y. Implied move is 6%.
DAL cost trends are worse (fuel and ex-fuel), while revenue trends are strong to better across airlines. Airlines are pushing price to capture or more than recapture higher jet fuel costs.
Upcoming reports: APOG and RPM reported pre-market on 10/6. CRH Q3 and full-year expectations are an inbound topic. TXT, DCO, and ORLY have upcoming company calls.
